newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former BoF member says EU economic govt needed.
newsitem.headline: Former BoF member says EU economic govt needed.

text.p: Europe needs an "economic government" to manage the European Union's (EU) economic affairs but not necessarily to counterbalance an independent European Central Bank (ECB), former Bank of France council member Jean Boissonnat, told afternoon daily Le Monde on Monday.
"A single currency completely modifies the landscape in terms of economic management. It is the last step of economic union and the first of political union," Boissonnat told Le Monde.
"Without a European economic government, the euro will be under the threat of explosion. I am not sure that European policymakers have realised the magnitude of the change we face."
He said the economic government would help minimise three major risks to economic union.
The first risk was overloading the ECB with management tasks that could lead to laying too much blame on the ECB for any problems in a single currency zone.

"We need to put a European economic government in place, not to counterbalance the power of the Bank or to reduce it, but to take over all the other tasks of economic management," the paper quoted him as saying.
He also expressed worry about over-compromising on the convergence criteria in the Maastricht Treaty, which he said could lead to the collapse of a single currency.
He said he believed the EU was unprepared to face problems arising from imbalances and shocks to individual countries within a single currency zone.
Boissonnat left the nine-member Bank of France policy setting council earlier this year.
